parole.significato: a bridge (construction that spans a divide)
parole.testo: From Old East Norse brō, from Proto-Germanic *brōwō (“bridge; brow”), possibly from Proto-Indo-European *bʰruH- (“beam; bridge”), which may be the same root as *h₃bʰrúHs (“(eye)brow”), whence bryn. Compare Norwegian Bokmål bro, Icelandic brú (“bridge”).
From Old Swedish buþ, from Old East Norse buð, from Proto-Germanic *budą (“offer, message”), cognate with Danish bud, Dutch bod, German Gebot.
Inherited from Old Swedish diūr, from Old East Norse diūʀ, from Proto-Germanic *deuzą, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰewsóm. Cognate with English deer and German Tier.
From Old Swedish iþer, idher, idhir, from Old East Norse *iðʀ (accusative/dative of *īʀ, East Norse form of ér), from Proto-Germanic *izwiz.
From Old Swedish fælder, from Old East Norse fældr (compare Old West Norse feldr), from Proto-Germanic *faldiz, from Proto-Indo-European *pel-. Related to fjäll (“scales”), päls (“furr”).

From Late Old Swedish ihiæl, from earlier Old Swedish i hæl, from Old East Norse ī hæl (Old West Norse í hel); compound of i (“in, to”) + hel (“the death, the underworld”), the latter cognate to hölja (“to cover”), from Proto-Germanic *haljō. Cognate with Danish ihjel and Norwegian Nynorsk i hel.

From Old Swedish krymplinger, (krymplinge, krimplinger), from a Old East Norse *krymplingʀ, from krympa (“to shrink”) + -lingʀ, ultimately to Proto-Germanic *krumpaz. Compare Swedish krypling, from Old Norse kryplingʀ; or Old Norse kryppill, from Proto-Germanic *krupilaz, from Proto-Indo-European *g
From Old Swedish siunka, from Old East Norse *siunkua, from Proto-Germanic *sinkwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *sengʷ- (“to fall, sink”).

From Old Swedish sō (Old Icelandic/Norwegian sýr), from Old East Norse *sōʀ, from Proto-Germanic *sūz, from Proto-Indo-European *sū-. Compare the identical ko (Old Icelandic/Norwegian kýr, Old Swedish kō).

From Old Swedish svamper, from Old East Norse svampr (compare Old West Norse svǫppr). Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *swampaz (“sponge, fungus”), variant of *swammaz. Probably a doublet of sopp and sump.

Inherited from Old Swedish søtma, oblique singular of søtme, from Old East Norse *sœtmi, *sǿtmi, from Proto-Germanic *swōtmô. Cognate of Norwegian Bokmål sødme and Old Frisian swētma. Equivalent to söt (“sweet”) + -ma; compare fetma.
From Old Swedish vīr, from Old East Norse *wīʀ (compare vér), from Proto-Germanic *wīz, from Proto-Indo-European *wéy, plural of *éǵh₂.

From Old Swedish vigge (“wedge”), from Old East Norse *viggʀ (compare Old West Norse veggr), from Proto-Germanic *wagjaz. Cognate of English wedge.
